conditions.name: Normal
conditions.summary: Sinus rhythm at the selected rate with coordinated contraction.
conditions.visual: Even chamber motion, valves fully closing, coronary flow unobstructed.

conditions.name: Coronary plaque
conditions.summary: Fatty and fibrous material narrows a coronary artery, reducing flow downstream.
conditions.visual: A pale narrowing in the proximal LAD with reduced flow beyond it.

conditions.name: Heart attack (ischaemia)
conditions.summary: A blocked coronary starves part of the muscle; that region stops contracting.
conditions.visual: A dusky, motionless patch in the LAD territory while the rest contracts.

conditions.name: Atrial fibrillation
conditions.summary: The atria quiver instead of contracting, and the ventricles are triggered irregularly.
conditions.visual: No organised atrial squeeze, irregular ventricular beats, no P wave.

conditions.name: Tachycardia
conditions.summary: A fast rhythm shortens filling time, so each beat moves less blood.
conditions.visual: Rapid beats with visibly reduced filling before each contraction.

conditions.name: Bradycardia
conditions.summary: A slow rhythm gives long filling times and a low output if it falls far enough.
conditions.visual: Slow, long diastoles with a large ventricular volume before each beat.

conditions.name: Heart block
conditions.summary: The signal is delayed or dropped between atria and ventricles.
conditions.visual: P waves continue but ventricular beats arrive late or are missed.

conditions.name: Valve stenosis
conditions.summary: A stiffened valve does not open fully, so the chamber behind it must push harder.
conditions.visual: A restricted opening with a visible pressure gradient and thicker upstream wall.

conditions.name: Valve leak
conditions.summary: A valve that does not seal lets blood flow backwards during contraction.
conditions.visual: A jet of reverse flow through a closed valve.

conditions.name: Heart failure
conditions.summary: A weak, often dilated ventricle cannot eject enough per beat.
conditions.visual: A large floppy ventricle with a small fractional shortening.

conditions.name: Left ventricular hypertrophy
conditions.summary: Chronic high afterload thickens the left ventricular wall, stiffening it.
conditions.visual: A visibly thicker left wall with a smaller cavity.

conditions.name: Septal defect
conditions.summary: A hole between the chambers lets blood cross from the higher-pressure side to the lower.
conditions.visual: A jet crossing the septum, with extra flow through the lungs.
